profile.reading:
Tahoe Reno 2 is one of the named future buildings on Switch's "Citadel Campus" in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Storey County, Nevada, adjacent to the Tesla Gigafactory. Switch's only public reference specifically naming Tahoe Reno 2 is a November 19, 2020 press release announcing that construction had been "accelerated" on the building, alongside site preparation beginning on the neighboring Tahoe Reno 3; that release did not give individual square footage, megawatt, or completion-date figures for either building, describing the full future campus build-out only in aggregate as "more than 7 million square feet and over 600 megawatts." Switch's FY2021 SEC 10-K filing, covering the period through December 31, 2021, lists the Citadel Campus portfolio as one current facility (Tahoe Reno 1) plus seven future facilities totaling 5.89 million gross square feet and 520 megawatts combined, without breaking that total out by individual building, meaning that as of Switch's last public-company financial disclosure, Tahoe Reno 2 had not yet opened and had no individually reported specifications. This OSM record shares the same 1 Superloop Circle address as Tahoe Reno 1 and the other numbered Tahoe Reno buildings in this dataset, consistent with all being part of one large campus rather than having individually distinct street addresses. Switch's current marketing describes the full Citadel Campus at up to 17.4 million square feet and more than 2 gigawatts of power at completion, a scale increase from the 2020-2021 figures reflecting continued campus expansion since Switch's 2022 acquisition by DigitalBridge and IFM Investors.

Storey County's Tahoe Reno Industrial Center spans roughly 107,000 acres and hosts more than 100 tenants beyond Switch, including Tesla's Gigafactory and Google, drawing more than 900 megawatts of on-site power generation capacity across the broader industrial park. Switch's 2020 press release describing accelerated construction on Tahoe Reno 2 specifically cited "multi-megawatt expansions with global e-commerce and semiconductor clients" as the demand driver behind the acceleration, tying this building's development timeline to named customer categories even though Switch has not disclosed which specific tenants occupy or are contracted for the building.

reading.body:
Tahoe Reno 2 is one of five buildings on Switch's Citadel Campus in Storey County, Nevada, a 107,000-acre industrial park that also hosts Tesla's Gigafactory and Google. Switch announced accelerated construction on this building in November 2020, citing demand from "global e-commerce and semiconductor clients" for multi-megawatt expansions, but has published no individual capacity figures for Tahoe Reno 2 itself. The only aggregate campus target Switch disclosed publicly was made in 2020 as "more than 7 million square feet and over 600 megawatts" across many buildings; that figure has since been updated in current marketing to 17.4 million square feet and more than 2 gigawatts at full build-out, reflecting continued expansion since Switch's 2022 acquisition by DigitalBridge and IFM Investors.

Tahoe Reno 2's individual specifications remain unpublished. Switch's last public financial filing, covering through December 2021, grouped the Citadel Campus's seven future facilities only in aggregate, reporting no breakdown by building. No completion date, square footage, or power capacity has been assigned to this facility in any published source consulted. The building's status as of late 2020 was "accelerated construction," but no subsequent operational date or occupancy status appears in published records.

Nevada has 26 mapped data center facilities and only 2 with published megawatt figures totaling 10.37 MW statewide, making Tahoe Reno 2's rank by published capacity meaningless since it contributes zero published figures to the state total. Whether Tahoe Reno 2 matters to AI infrastructure depends entirely on when Switch publishes its specifications; until then, it is invisible to any grid-constrained analysis of compute capacity.
